mentions.name: Memex
mentions.description: Memex is a personal work-memory tool with a CLI interface and MCP support that records what you have worked on so you can quickly answer questions like "what did I work on last week?" or find a Hacker News post about compiler optimization you forgot to bookmark. It connects to Claude via MCP to provide work context for tasks such as tailoring a resume to a specific job application, reviewing the past week of work to surface unfinished tasks, and recalling how a server set up a month ago was configured (exportable as a .md file). It replaces the author's use of bookmarks and lists/bug tracking. The name comes from Vannevar Bush's 1945 "As We May Think" concept of a personal, mechanized filing system supplementing memory.
mentions.problem: The author realized they had no history of what they had worked on in the past, making it hard to recall past work or retrieve forgotten saved content.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm working on Memex: https://github.com/joenewbry/memex

It's inspired by a moment a few years ago when I realized I had no history of what I had worked on in the past.
